name: LSPatch patcher
notes: What the manager is: its assets/ are the injection runtime the manager writes into the target APK, and its Java classes (minus the one class this repository vendors) are the patcher the manager drives. android/manager/build.gradle splits the two halves and excludes org/lsposed/patch/ApkPatcher.class in favour of the vendored source. The digest is upstream's own pinned release, unchanged.

name: Xposed API
notes: Compile-only for the loader: every loader source imports de.robv.android.xposed.*, and the classes are provided by the process the loader is injected into, so they must not be packaged. Staged rather than resolved from a Maven repository, because JCenter - where the coordinate lived - no longer serves new resolutions.

name: Revenge runtime bundle
notes: The runtime the loader injects, downloaded unchanged and patched by scripts/patch_runtime.py into assets/assault-runtime.js, which is also the asset the 16 MiB cap is written for. It is what hooks the client and builds the Addons, Themes and Code runner pages. This is the path patch_runtime.py reads by name; the asset name stays assault-runtime.js because the loader's Java loads that name and renaming a file is not a rebrand.

name: Storage hook patch text
source: this repository (the reviewed patch text patch_runtime.py splices into the runtime)
notes: Checked in, so there is nothing to fetch and no upstream digest to pin; it is listed because patch_runtime.py reads it by name and a missing one fails the loader's runtimeAssets task with a FileNotFoundError.

name: Gradle wrapper distribution
notes: Checked in so ./gradlew works; the distribution it downloads is pinned by distributionSha256Sum in gradle/wrapper/gradle-wrapper.properties. Listed with no URL on purpose: it is not fetched by scripts/fetch_android_deps.py, and claiming a digest for a file already in the tree would be a check nothing performs.

name: Bundled addons for the loader
source: generated by scripts/build_addons.mjs from core/, utils/, plugins/ and themes/
notes: The asset that carries Hypercord's own plugins and themes into the APK. It is generated, not fetched, so it has no URL - `npm run build:addons` writes it - and scripts/build_android.py refuses to build an APK while the file is still the placeholder, because an APK with the placeholder installs, reports nothing wrong and has no plugins in it.
